mainEntity.name: How much does a Mini Countryman Cooper S E ALL4 PHEV engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost depends on the engine condition and hybrid system complexity. For the B38A15A PHEV unit, a used engine typically costs £2,000-£3,500 (supply only), while a fully reconditioned or rebuilt engine with a warranty ranges from £3,500 to £7,500 (supply only).

mainEntity.name: What are the early signs of hybrid engine failure in a Mini Countryman Cooper S E ALL4 PHEV?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning signs include persistent coolant level warnings, hybrid system fault lights on the dashboard, or a noticeable loss of electric-only driving range.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in an older F60 Mini Countryman Cooper S E ALL4 PHEV?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's current market value and overall condition. F60 models typically value between £12,000 and £22,000. If the car is worth under £15,000, a used engine or major preventative repair may be the most financially viable option.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mini Countryman Cooper S E ALL4 PHEV engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional supply and fit service for a Mini Countryman Cooper S E ALL4 PHEV typically takes 2 to 4 working days due to hybrid system complexity. Sourcing a quality reconditioned or rebuilt PHEV engine may take a few days if not immediately available.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the Mini Countryman Cooper S E ALL4 PHEV and standard Cooper engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: While both are petrol variants, the Cooper S E ALL4 PHEV integrates a 1.5L turbocharged engine with a rear-axle electric motor for all-wheel drive, unlike the front-wheel-drive standard Cooper. The PHEV variant features a reinforced drivetrain, a high-voltage battery pack, and a dedicated hybrid cooling circuit.

problems.group: EGR Cooler & Hybrid Cooling System Leaks
problems.h4: EGR Cooler & Hybrid Cooling System Leaks - Mini Countryman Cooper S E ALL4 PHEV Vulnerabilities
problems.affectedModels: Mini Countryman Cooper S E ALL4 PHEV (B38A15A + eDrive, 2017-present)
problems.rootCause: The B38 engine's plastic EGR cooler is prone to internal cracking, while the separate high-voltage battery cooling circuit can develop pump or seal failures. This leads to coolant loss, potential hybrid system contamination, and subsequent limp mode.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace EGR cooler, high-voltage coolant pump, and flush both systems.
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if caught early with no internal engine damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of a rebuilt B38A15A PHEV unit with updated cooling components and 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary if coolant ingress has caused internal corrosion or hybrid system damage.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Mini Countryman Cooper S E ALL4 PHEV falls into distinct value bands depending on generation: F60 models range from £12,000-£22,000, while newer U25 models command £28,000-£40,000+ `[THIRD-PARTY]`. - Vehicle worth under ~£15,000 (older F60): Evaluate carefully; a used engine or specialist preventative repair may be more financially viable than a full rebuilt unit, as replacement costs can approach 40-50% of the vehicle's value. - Vehicle worth £15,000-£40,000+ (late F60 / U25): A reconditioned or rebuilt engine is a highly viable investment. The replacement cost is a small fraction of the vehicle's value, and the 12-month warranty restores long-term reliability.
problems.recommendation: For early cooling system warnings, a specialist overhaul of the EGR and hybrid cooling circuits is the most cost-effective route. However, if the engine has suffered catastrophic overheating or hybrid system contamination, a rebuilt engine is the only reliable long-term solution. Do not ignore high-voltage or coolant warning lights.
